paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Israel's whole identity rests on the LORD's love, not on Israel's strength. Moses says, "For you are a people holy to the LORD your God." (Deuteronomy 7:6) Then he says they were "the fewest of all peoples," and that the LORD chose them "because the LORD loved you and kept the oath He swore to your fathers." (Deuteronomy 7:7-8)

So everything else in the chapter flows out of that love. The LORD is "the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations of those who love Him and keep His commandments." (Deuteronomy 7:9) That's why Moses calls Israel to keep His commands and to stay away from other gods, because those gods would be "a snare" to them. (Deuteronomy 7:11, 16) Moses is not asking Israel to earn love they already have. He's asking them to stay close to the One who loved them first.

And when the fear shows up, and it will, Moses gives Israel one cure: remember. "Do not be afraid of them. Be sure to remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt." (Deuteronomy 7:18) Your giants may look bigger than you, baker, but the LORD is "among you," and He is "a great and awesome God." (Deuteronomy 7:21) When you're scared, look back at what He has already done, then take the next step with Him. The story isn't over, because Moses is NOT done preaching.
